brief: Compare fictional account costs and access conditions against an explicitly stated pattern of use.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Account costs"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Compara condiciones de cuentas"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Compare condições de contas"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Compare fictional account costs and access conditions against an explicitly stated pattern of use.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: An account can have several kinds of cost. Compare the operations you actually need and when you need them.
instruction.misconception: Treating a no-monthly-fee headline as proof that all operations are free or all access needs are met.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use only the stated quantities, dates and conditions; distinguish a modeled result from a guarantee.

evidence.reasoning: Fictional account A charges per withdrawal, without monthly fees. Account B charges monthly and includes those withdrawals.
Calculate each account cost for the same planned operations. Then check access times, restrictions and any conditions for fee waivers.
A monthly-fee statement does not price every operation.
Equal use makes the totals comparable.
A conditional benefit applies only under its stated conditions.
A low cost does not fix an incompatible access time.
Spending permission can create debt rather than new income.
Changed use can change the relevant costs and conditions.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Apply this skill in a later integrated decision with a different constraint.
